turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I came in because... I don't know, things have just been really off lately. Ever since I moved into this busted-up room I'm renting, I've just been snapping at people. I end up staying up half the night trying to fix leaks or messing with the heat because it's always broken. Then I'm just dragging myself into work late, and I'm messing up on the job—stuff I normally handle with no problem at all. It's just getting to be too much.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing emotional and behavioral difficulties (snapping at people, work impairment, staying up late) directly in response to an identifiable stressor (moving into a substandard rental room).

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or seeing friends?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I mean, I still want to hang out with my buddies and do my normal stuff. It's just... I haven't really had the time or the energy for it lately. Between being at the site all day and then coming back to deal with the apartment all night, I'm just too beat to actually go out. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest in it or anything.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest in hobbies or seeing friends, stating they still want to do normal activities and hang out with friends but are just too busy and tired.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't feel sad or depressed most of the day. I mean, I'm definitely frustrated, you know? Like I said, I'm mostly just tired and pissed off about the apartment always being broken. But I'm not walking around feeling down or crying all the time or anything like that. It's just a lot of stress right now.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad, depressed, or crying, stating they do not feel down or depressed most of the day.

turns.doctor_question: Would you say you’ve been more irritable or easily angered lately, even over small things?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. Like I mentioned earlier, I've just been snapping at people. It really doesn't take much right now to set me off. A guy at the site will just ask me a normal question, or I'll, I don't know, drop a tool or something, and I just get really ticked off. I guess I just have a really short fuse right now since I'm running on empty with the whole apartment situation.

symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient explicitly confirms being irritable, having a short fuse, and snapping at others over minor occurrences.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any particularly traumatic or highly stressful events recently, beyond the problems with your apartment, that might be contributing to how you're feeling?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. It's really just the apartment. I mean, work is work, it's always physical and tiring, but that's normal. There hasn't been any big tragedy or, you know, major crisis besides just dealing with the constant issues at my place. That's the only thing that's really changed lately.

turns.doctor_question: Has your irritability or stress been affecting your relationships with others or your ability to work effectively?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it definitely is. I mean, my foreman actually pulled me aside recently. He basically told me I could lose my shot at moving up to crew lead if I keep slipping up and snapping at people. And it's not just the attitude stuff... I've already messed up some work paperwork and had scheduling problems because I'm just so distracted by all this apartment crap. It's definitely bleeding into my job.

symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient confirms irritability affecting work, noting they have been 'snapping at people' and showing snappiness/low frustration tolerance.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your irritability and stress mainly happen when you're dealing with the apartment problems, or do you feel this way even when those issues aren’t on your mind?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure, honestly. It feels like... well, the apartment stuff is just always in the back of my head right now. So even if I'm at work and not actively dealing with it, I'm still stressed out about it. I haven't really noticed a time when it's completely off my mind, so it's hard to say. It just kind of hangs over me all day.

turns.doctor_question: Can you recall any moments in the past week where you felt irritable or stressed when you weren’t thinking about the apartment or its problems?
turns.patient_response: Not really. Like I said, it's just... it's always there. I can't think of a single time in the past week where I wasn't at least a little bit worried about what else is going to break or how I'm going to deal with the landlord. So, no, I don't think there's been a time where I was stressed about something completely different. It all comes back to the apartment right now.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms that their persistent stress and worry are entirely centered on an identifiable stressor (the apartment problems and landlord).

turns.doctor_question: If the apartment issues were suddenly resolved, do you think your irritability and stress would go away, or do you think they would stick around?
turns.patient_response: I'm pretty sure it would go away. I mean, the housing mess hasn't really ended yet—I'm still living in that room and still dealing with the repairs and the landlord every day. So it's not like this is something that just kept going long after the problem was over. I'm still right in the middle of it. But yeah, if it actually got resolved and I didn't have to worry about it anymore, I think I'd go back to normal.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms their stress and emotional symptoms are directly tied to an ongoing identifiable stressor (housing repairs and landlord issues) and expects them to resolve once the situation is fixed.
